citation.title: Research on topology optimization of carbon fiber reinforced composite electric vehicle helmet based on deep learning
citation.authors: Xiangkui Zhang, Wei Wei, Ping Hu, Chengxiang Han
citation.venue: Journal of Physics: Conference Series 2791 (2024) 012064, CMSDA-2023 proceedings (IOP Publishing; open access, CC BY 4.0 per the article's first page)
citation.version_coded: Version of record, IOP publisher PDF (14 pp.: IOP cover page plus printed pp. 1-13) from iopscience.iop.org, read in full as text. Page locators below are the printed page numbers. The adjudicator re-read the same PDF in full on 2026-09-24: a plain curl request to the Crossref-listed PDF link (iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1742-6596/2791/1/012064/pdf) was redirected to IOP's bot check and was not pursued; a single request to the same link through the session's web-fetch tool (whose User-Agent string the adjudicator does not set) was served the PDF directly, with no challenge shown (CC BY 4.0 per Crossref and the first page)

included.reason: I-QUALITY (screened I-UNCLEAR; the only quantitative comparison with a classical result is the network's loss against SIMP labels on the held-out verification set; no time of any method is reported)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: A modified U-Net trained on SIMP designs of the flattened helmet grids (30,000 samples in all, split 8:1:1) reproduces the SIMP element densities with a mean-squared-error loss of about 0.005 on the training set and 0.01 on the held-out verification set after 100 epochs.
claim.location: Sec. 3.3, p. 7, Eq. 13 and Fig. 10 (first quantitative comparison with classical results, in the main text; §5.1 rule 2). The abstract, introduction and conclusion compare the optimized helmet only with an unoptimized ABS helmet, and the conclusion's speed statements are qualitative
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not derivable: no time of any method is reported. The conclusion states only qualitatively that the 2D reduction is faster than working on the 3D model and that the network skips the iterative FE calculation (Sec. 6, p. 12). SIMP data generation in MATLAB (30,000 samples) is not timed (p. 5).
claim.alternatives: (1) Abstract, Sec. 5.2 and Fig. 22 (pp. 10-12): at equal mass (0.33 kg) the optimized CFRP helmet shows 7 mm vs 19 mm maximum extrusion displacement and 167 g vs 369 g peak collision acceleration against an ordinary ABS helmet; the comparator is an unoptimized product in another material, not a classical optimizer. (2) Sec. 6, qualitative: the dimension-reduced optimization is faster and easier than optimizing the 3D model, and the network gives the structure directly without FE iterations; nothing is run or timed for either statement.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP (variable density) compliance minimization, used only to generate the training labels: penalty 3, filter radius 1.5, volume fraction 0.3-0.7, random nodal loads of -150 to 150 N in x and y on the free edges, four edge-constraint variants, plus a fixed middle region for the top grid (Sec. 3.1, pp. 4-5)
baseline.implementation: MATLAB code based on the variable density method (p. 2 and p. 5); the 99-line and 88-line codes are cited for the method (refs [9], [10]); the exact code is not stated
baseline.hardware_ml: Intel Xeon Gold 6248R CPU with three NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPUs, TensorFlow (Sec. 3.3, p. 7)
baseline.problem_size: 2D flattened helmet grids of 85×35, 79×35 and 85×79 quadrilateral elements (element size 2.5) (Sec. 2.2 p. 3, Sec. 3.1 p. 5); network inputs 85×35×6 element and 86×36×4 nodal tensors, output 85×35×1 (Sec. 3.2, p. 6) [derived: about 6.2×10³ DOFs for 85×35 and 1.4×10⁴ for 85×79]
baseline.training_time: not stated; 100 epochs, Adam optimizer, initial learning rate 0.001, MSE loss (Sec. 3.3, p. 7)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; 30,000 SIMP samples over all cases, split 8:1:1 into training, verification and test sets (Sec. 3.1, p. 5)
baseline.quality_metric: Mean-squared-error loss between predicted and SIMP element densities on the training and verification sets (Eq. 13, Fig. 10). The final 3D helmet is checked by ABAQUS extrusion (maximum displacement) and collision (peak acceleration) simulations against an ordinary ABS helmet (Sec. 5.2)
baseline.quality_gap: Loss falls from 0.08 to 0.005 (training) and from 0.06 to 0.01 (verification) over 100 epochs (p. 7, Fig. 10). No test-set metric, compliance or volume of predicted designs is compared with SIMP. Helmet vs ordinary ABS helmet at 0.33 kg: displacement 7 vs 19 mm; acceleration 167 g vs 369 g (pp. 11-12)

R1.evidence: Sec. 3.1 and 3.3, Fig. 10: predictions and SIMP labels come from the same problem generator (held-out verification split), so the problem settings match, but agreement is measured only as an MSE loss. The compliance and volume fraction of predicted designs are not reported, the SIMP stopping rule is not stated, and no time or FE budget is matched.

R2.evidence: No speed or cost comparison is quantified: no classical time, iteration count or hardware is reported (Sec. 3.1, 3.3), so criteria (a)-(e) cannot apply. The SIMP labels come from a MATLAB code built on the cited 99-line and 88-line educational codes [inferred from p. 2, p. 5 and refs 9-10]. Stratum Q (PROTOCOL §11, 2026-09-24): the abstract (p. 1) names SIMP only as the data generator and gives no baseline figures, so criterion (b) is not observed.

R3.evidence: The only speed statements are qualitative (Sec. 6, p. 12). For C3: neither the cost of the 30,000 SIMP samples (p. 5) nor the training time (100 epochs on three RTX 3090 GPUs, p. 7) is reported; no break-even is given.

R4.evidence: Sec. 3.3 and Fig. 10: agreement with SIMP rests only on the MSE loss of element densities. No FE analysis of a predicted 2D design, no volume check and no failure count are reported. The 3D helmet is FE-analysed in ABAQUS (Sec. 5.2) only after the stiffeners were modified by hand to remove checkerboard regions (p. 9, Figs. 15-16), and only against an ordinary ABS helmet.

reporting.n_test_cases: 30,000 samples split 8:1:1 (p. 5) [derived: about 3,000 verification and 3,000 test samples]; only training and verification losses are reported (Fig. 10), no test-set result; one helmet application (Sec. 4-5)

notes: Stratum judgment for the verifier: the only quantitative comparison with a classical result is the verification-set MSE against the SIMP labels (Sec. 3.3, Fig. 10). It is coded stratum Q, as test-set similarity to TO designs was coded in P00165. Alternative: FT-NOBASELINE, if a training and validation loss curve is not counted as a comparison. The article never times SIMP, never compares the compliance or volume of any predicted design with SIMP, and its only design-level comparison is with an unoptimized ABS helmet in another material. Exclusion codes checked in order: no duplicate (the other pool record with Xiangkui Zhang, P01865, is a different CWGAN study); in scope (a network produces TO layouts for linear-elastic compliance); a conference method paper (CMSDA-2023); not an excluded domain; the network produces designs, so not forward-only; no ML comparator. ood_test = unclear: the helmet inputs come from a 3D FE analysis with fixed sides and 150 N loads at the front, back, left, right and top (Sec. 4.1, p. 8), unlike the 2D cantilever generator [inferred], but the helmet prediction is not checked against SIMP. Post-processing: the 2D prediction is mapped to 3D and the stiffeners are modified by hand for checkerboard regions (pp. 9-10, Figs. 14-16). Internal inconsistencies: Table 1's caption is template text ('Formatting sections, subsections, and subsubsections', p. 2); the top grid is called 85×79 and 89×79 (p. 5); Figs. 20-21 are captioned as extrusion experiments but belong to the collision test (p. 11); the Fig. 10 caption says test set, the text says verification set (p. 7). No code or data statement. No author named Jun Wang. Screening code was I-UNCLEAR (decision order position 110).

access.reason: The first coder's route works: the IOP version-of-record PDF (Crossref VOR link, CC BY 4.0, 14 pp.) was served without a challenge to one web-fetch request on 2026-09-24, and the adjudicator read it in full. The second coder met IOP's bot check on the DOI route and rightly stopped there; the adjudicator's own curl request met the same check, and that route was dropped without any bypass.

stratum.reason: The abstract (p. 1) and conclusion (Sec. 6, p. 12) compare only with an ordinary ABS helmet or state speed qualitatively, so §5.1 rule 2 takes the main text's first quantitative classical comparison: the verification-set MSE of 0.01 against SIMP labels (Sec. 3.3, p. 7, Fig. 10). That compares design quality only, as for P00165.

R1.reason: R1 applies as written in stratum Q (§11). Predictions and SIMP labels share the generator's instances (Sec. 3.1, p. 5), but agreement is only an MSE loss, the volume and compliance of predicted designs are never reported, and the SIMP stopping rule is unstated (Sec. 3.3, p. 7): the §5.3 R1 partial case.

R2.reason: Stratum Q (§11): R2 applies only through criterion (b). The abstract (p. 1) gives no baseline figures and names SIMP only as the data generator, and no classical time or setting is reported anywhere (Secs. 3.1, 3.3), so (b) is not observed.

R3.reason: Stratum Q (§11): R3 concerns speed claims, and the article's speed statements are qualitative only (Sec. 6, p. 12).

R4.reason: Agreement with SIMP rests only on the element-density MSE (Eq. 13, Fig. 10, p. 7), an image-similarity metric. No predicted 2D design is FE-analysed or volume-checked; the ABAQUS runs (Sec. 5.2, pp. 10-12) test the hand-modified helmet (Figs. 15-16, p. 10) against an ordinary helmet, not against SIMP.
